title: One Bar Over the Map
userRequest: Project context: A conversational AI tool that helps people turn vague ideas and problems into clear, structured, actionable plans. It will need to be an MCP
description:
The chat panel that floated over the board is hidden, and a bar took its place: it counts what is still waiting, flies the camera to the next unanswered card when you press the count, lists every open question by its own words behind a chevron, and carries Chat, the way on to the next phase, and a round trip to the far end of the map badged with what arrived while you were answering. Its one rule is that the left side ALWAYS POINTS SOMEWHERE — it briefly read 'Nothing waiting on you' beside two other controls each claiming to be the next move, which is the dead end the rule now exists to prevent. The answer card grew (360 to 460 board units) and stopped making you choose: shortlist options TOGGLE so several can be taken, the free-text box sits beside them rather than replacing them, one Save records the combination, Skip moves you on without answering so the question stays open, and after saving the card turns over to show your words before the board carries you to the next one. The far end stopped being a separate screen and stopped calling itself a finish line: 'I didn't build the product yet' is gone, and what stands where the map's rows converge is Insights & experiments — things you could try with what each would settle, directions you can take as buttons, what is being learned, what is still open, and a way back into the loop. Every way forward can now state what it would take and what taking it would cost, through a new MapNode.tradeoffs column and a matching field in the agent's tool schema: two bullets on the card and the rest behind 'Dig in', printed as the partner wrote them because a rough estimate someone can argue with beats a number that only looks computed.

SCOPE VERDICT — DELIVERED: nothing new from the project's deliverable list, because all nine build deliverables were already delivered in earlier cycles; this cycle refines three of them ('a live visual map that grows as the conversation develops', 'a final actionable output', and 'after the plan is produced, keep discussing and working'), the last of those most directly, since the plan is no longer a screen you leave the map to read. DEFERRED: none by this cycle. One deliverable remains deferred from an earlier one — registering the MCP server in a client such as Claude Desktop — which the user themselves confirmed at that cycle's plan gate as assist-track work (machine configuration and a walkthrough, not code). Every other row is `decidedBy: agent` and every one of those is marked delivered, so no agent-decided deferral is hiding in this trail.

COVERAGE LOST, deliberately and at the user's instruction: the 'Next round' button was removed, and with it the visible countdown you could cancel by typing. The round still ends itself and typing in the bar still holds it open, but two scenarios existed to demonstrate the cancel — boardworkspace-roundheldopen and the-round-ends-itself-on-a-real-board — and with nothing left on screen to photograph they were retired rather than left asserting something the app no longer shows.

STALE DOCUMENTATION, not fixed here: design_system.md section 4 still describes the retired scrolling-column map and says pan/zoom were removed, and section 7 still names 'I DIDN'T BUILD THE PRODUCT YET.' as the product's voice. Both were already wrong about the shipped board before this cycle; the second is now wrong because of it. Naming them so the next reader does not follow the doc into a design the app abandoned.
